publisher_issuer: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (uscourts.gov)
company_context: The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts publishes official US bankruptcy filing statistics on a rolling 12-month basis. This release reports totals for the 12-month period ending December 31, 2025, including business and Chapter 11 breakdowns, providing authoritative base rates for business insolvency.
business_type: US bankruptcy court system aggregate filings (business and non-business); population-level dataset, not a single company
evidence_summary: For the 12-month period ending December 31, 2025, total US bankruptcy filings reached 574,314, up from 517,308 the prior year. Business filings rose 7.1%, from 23,107 to 24,737. Non-business filings rose 11.2% to 549,577 (from 494,201). Chapter 11 filings dropped 1% to 8,937; business Chapter 11 petitions decreased 2% to 8,405, amounting to 35% of all business cases filed. Filings are reported quarterly for each 12-month period ending March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31. These are authoritative base rates for how often businesses reach formal insolvency.
outcome_evidence: Population-level dataset, not a single-firm outcome: documents the volume and year-over-year change of US business and Chapter 11 bankruptcy filings for the 12 months ending December 31, 2025.
source_limitations: Aggregate count data, not company-specific causation; figures captured from uscourts.gov result snippets (page not fetched directly). Counts are filings, not adjudicated outcomes, and do not attribute cause.
directly_stated: Total filings 574,314 (12 months ending Dec 2025), up from 517,308
Business Chapter 11 petitions 8,405, down 2%, 35% of all business cases
Filings reported quarterly for 12-month periods ending Mar 31/Jun 30/Sep 30/Dec 31
inferred: Formal business insolvency remains a low-probability terminal event relative to the total small-business population
Year-over-year increases indicate rising debt/solvency pressure in the economy
why_useful_for_opsiq: Authoritative base rates for business and Chapter 11 bankruptcy frequency. Useful for calibrating OpsIQ priors on how likely a distressed firm is to actually reach formal insolvency, so debt_solvency_pressure diagnoses are weighted against realistic terminal-event rates rather than over-predicting bankruptcy.
